summary: K8s admission annotation rollback during KMS rewrap prevents runner credential injection; CI jobs stuck in Pending
description: Summary: During a scheduled KMS key rewrap for signing customer service-account keys, an automated annotation mutation performed by the CI credential injector was rolled back by a stale admission-controller config. The result: newly scheduled runner pods booted without the credential-injection annotation, failed attestation to runner-manager, and left pipeline jobs Pending for >20 minutes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a KMS rewrap job that updates credential metadata (internal routine triggered at 03:00 UTC).

2) CI credential-injector controller performs a pod admission mutation to add annotation 'ci.redwood.com/cred-version: v2' and mounts secret volume, then requests a rolling restart via pod mutation webhook.
3) Due to a race, kube-admission config from an older control-plane instance reverted the admission webhook changes for ~10% of pods (annotation omitted).
4) Runner-manager sees the pod but cannot validate the attestation header (missing injected secret), marks runner as Unhealthy, and does not accept jobs. Pipelines queue and stay in Pending.
5) Observed at scale with multiple namespaces and several CI queues impacted concurrently.
observed_behavior: Runner pods scheduled and Running but without the credential annotation and secret mounts; runner-manager logs show 'attestation failed: missing-credential'; CI pipelines show jobs stuck in Pending with 'no available runners'.
expected_behavior: After KMS rewrap and injector mutations, all runner pods should be annotated with the new credential version and mount the corresponding secret; attestation should succeed and jobs should be scheduled immediately.

comments: 2026-03-10T04:10Z - Samir Patel: Initial triage done — spike shows ~12% of new runner pods lacked cred annotation between 03:05-03:20 UTC. Opening incident. Prioritized rollback plan ready.

2026-03-10T05:02Z - Lina Gomez (SRE): Confirmed kube-apiserver leader had stale webhook config from prior deploy; propagated to 2x control-plane instances after canary. Rolling restart of control-plane fixed propagation.

2026-03-10T05:45Z - Maya Chen: Applied emergency patch to credential-injector to be idempotent and to double-check secret mounts post-admission. Requeued stuck pipelines; jobs drained over 15 minutes.
2026-03-11T09:30Z - Samir Patel: Postmortem draft around config rollout ordering added; follow-ups tracked under INT-53278 (config-deploy-safety-checks).
investigation_notes: Root cause: race between new injector webhook config (v2) and partial rollback of webhook configs on two control-plane replicas during a separate config-operator reconcile. The rollback removed a required mutating rule for a subset of admission requests.

Why it caused runner impact: runner pods rely on the mutating webhook to attach secrets at creation time. Without the annotation and secret mount attestation fails and runner-manager refuses to accept the pod as a healthy runner.
Scope: ~120 runner pods impacted across 4 namespaces, representing ~18% of CI queue capacity in us-east1 for the 15-minute window.

Mitigations attempted: immediate control-plane rolling restart (partial), emergency reapply of webhook CRD, forced pod restart for affected runners, and manual secret re-injection for high-priority namespaces.
mitigation: Immediate: Reapplied correct webhook config and performed rolling restart of control-plane instances — fixed propagation mismatch.
Short-term: Implemented a post-admission verification in the credential-injector: if a pod misses the annotation, controller patches it and triggers a restart.
Workaround for customers: Support command 'cictl runners requeue --namespace <ns>' to restart stuck runner pods in affected namespaces.
resolution: Permanent fix: config-operator was updated to include an ordered rollout guard and a locking mechanism to prevent concurrent CRD rewrites. Credential-injector was hardened to be idempotent and to verify mounts after admission. Monitoring was added (synthetic pod creation checks) to detect missing annotations within 30s of pod creation. All affected pipelines were requeued and drained. Incident closed.
